```{r}
# =============================================================================
# Italian Serie A historical match data scraper
# Source: https://football-data.co.uk/
#
# Output: serie_a_matches
# Columns: Season, Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG
# =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(readr)
library(purrr)
library(lubridate)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Generate season identifiers from 1993/94 through the current season
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

today <- Sys.Date()
current_year <- lubridate::year(today)
current_month <- lubridate::month(today)

# Seasons start in the second half of the calendar year.
# Before July, the current season began in the previous calendar year.
season_start_year <- if (current_month >= 7L) {
  current_year
} else {
  current_year - 1L
}

# Convert a starting year to the four-digit season identifier.
# Example: 1993 -> "9394"
make_season_id <- function(start_year) {
  sprintf(
    "%02d%02d",
    start_year %% 100L,
    (start_year + 1L) %% 100L
  )
}

season_start_years <- seq.int(1993L, season_start_year)

seasons <- vapply(
  season_start_years,
  make_season_id,
  character(1)
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Parse source dates robustly
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

parse_match_dates <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  x[x == ""] <- NA_character_
  
  # Source files may use dd/mm/yy, dd/mm/yyyy, or ISO yyyy-mm-dd.
  # Explicit formats avoid locale-dependent date parsing.
  parsed <- suppressWarnings(
    lubridate::parse_date_time(
      x,
      orders = c("dmy", "ymd"),
      quiet = TRUE,
      truncated = 0
    )
  )
  
  as.Date(parsed)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Download and process a single season
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

download_season <- function(season) {
  
  url <- sprintf(
    "https://football-data.co.uk/mmz4281/%s/I1.csv",
    season
  )
  
  message("Downloading season ", season, ": ", url)
  
  # Read directly from the remote CSV. Explicit encoding accommodates
  # accented team names in legacy source files.
  raw_data <- tryCatch(
    readr::read_csv(
      file = url,
      col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
      locale = locale(encoding = "Latin1"),
      na = c("", "NA", "N/A"),
      trim_ws = TRUE,
      show_col_types = FALSE,
      progress = FALSE,
      name_repair = "minimal"
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      message(
        "Skipping season ", season, " (download/read error): ",
        conditionMessage(e)
      )
      return(NULL)
    }
  )
  
  if (is.null(raw_data)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  required_columns <- c(
    "Date", "HomeTeam", "AwayTeam", "FTHG", "FTAG"
  )
  
  missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(raw_data))
  
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {
    message(
      "Skipping season ", season, "; missing columns: ",
      paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
    )
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  processed <- raw_data %>%
    select(all_of(required_columns)) %>%
    mutate(
      Date = parse_match_dates(Date),
      HomeTeam = as.character(HomeTeam),
      AwayTeam = as.character(AwayTeam),
      FTHG = suppressWarnings(as.integer(FTHG)),
      FTAG = suppressWarnings(as.integer(FTAG)),
      Season = as.character(season)
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Date)) %>%
    select(Season, Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG) %>%
    arrange(Date)
  
  message(
    "Season ", season, ": ",
    nrow(processed), " matches with valid dates."
  )
  
  as_tibble(processed)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Retrieve all seasons and combine the results
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

season_data <- purrr::map(seasons, download_season)

# map_dfr() safely combines successful results, ignoring NULL entries.
serie_a_matches <- purrr::map_dfr(
  season_data,
  ~ if (is.null(.x)) NULL else .x
) %>%
  mutate(
    Season = as.character(Season),
    Date = as.Date(Date),
    HomeTeam = as.character(HomeTeam),
    AwayTeam = as.character(AwayTeam),
    FTHG = as.integer(FTHG),
    FTAG = as.integer(FTAG)
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    match(Season, seasons),
    Date
  ) %>%
  select(Season, Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG) %>%
  as_tibble()

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Report the results
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

message(
  "\nCompleted. Retrieved ",
  nrow(serie_a_matches),
  " matches across ",
  dplyr::n_distinct(serie_a_matches$Season),
  " seasons."
)

print(serie_a_matches)

# Optional: inspect the structure and season coverage.
glimpse(serie_a_matches)

serie_a_matches %>%
  count(Season, name = "Matches") %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```
